pages.text: "I will play until sunset!" Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, ran down the snowy alley. A foot caught on a snowball. Down went Kiki!
Snow slipped down the back of the neck. Cold! "Ah, so cold!" Kiki stamped both feet. The face turned red.
Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, stepped back in surprise. Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, shut his eyes. The lively alley fell quiet.
Grandpa Badger stood his broom upright. "Kiki, squeeze a handful of snow." He scooped some into Kiki's hand.
Kiki squeezed tightly, hands trembling. "Now, squeeze some snow, breathe out!" Grandpa blew a long breath. Kiki copied.
Kiki opened the hand. Melted snow dripped down. The hot feeling in the chest cooled too. "The anger came out through my hand!" Kiki looked at the palm.
Kiki came to Nono. "My loud shouting scared you too, right? I am all right now." Nono hopped up and held Kiki's hand.
Kiki touched the green bell. Jingle! Laughter returned to the quiet alley. They ran, crunching through snow.
Soon Kiki's snowball crumbled. Anger crept back. Kiki quickly grabbed snow. "Squeeze—breathe out! Open your hand!" The anger slipped away.
Nono and Gugu hugged Kiki from either side. Feeling angry is not bad. A long breath can let it drift away. Kiki opened both hands. "Squeeze some snow, breathe out!"
